import sys, json, datetime

# The incoming message and this cell's OWN configuration arrive on the same
# stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects, beside
# `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there is
# nothing to hand over). Every knob below is read from it, so each one is
# per-INSTANCE configuration -- two keepers in one colony end their sessions on
# different rules, and a mutation retunes one of them without touching a
# colony-wide environment. The literal beside each name is the shipped default;
# it is the same value the template config and `contract.settings` carry, and a
# test pins the three against each other.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


def _hhmm(key, default):
    """A time of the UTC day, "HH:MM", as minutes since midnight; "24:00" is
    the end of the day. Blank falls back like the numbers above."""
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        v = default
    hh, mm = str(v).strip().split(":")
    return int(hh) * 60 + int(mm)


# --- the idle rule (deterministic arithmetic, never a model judgement) ------
# A session ends the way a phone call ends: nobody said anything for a while,
# and it is night. Both halves are configuration -- the night is the window
# below, the silence is this threshold.
IDLE_MS = _int("idle_ms", 7200000)
# Runaway guard of the sweep: a store select has no implicit limit.
CLOSE_LIMIT = _int("close_limit", 50)
# How many sealed rows one heal page visits (GH #954). Read like close_limit.
HEAL_LIMIT = _int("heal_limit", 200)
# The night, R-AG-1 (GH #1229): the window [from, until) of the UTC day in which
# a silent generation may end. It crosses midnight when from > until; from ==
# until is no night at all, and then the keeper arms nothing (an `in_sweep`
# still sweeps). The defaults are 00:00-06:00 Europe/Berlin in summer (CEST,
# UTC+2); winter (CET, UTC+1) is "23:00" until "05:00". UTC = local - offset.
NIGHT_FROM = _hhmm("night_from_utc", "22:00")
NIGHT_UNTIL = _hhmm("night_until_utc", "04:00")
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
phase = str(ctx.get("ses_phase", ""))
lane = str(hop.get("route", ""))
op = hop.get("operation")
# `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it worked, and
# both have to be read (GH #343).
err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")
rows_affected = int(hop.get("rows_affected", 0) or 0)
channel = str(ctx.get("channel", "") or "")
session = str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or "")
# The round the sealed generation was spoken in, read off its own row in the
# sweep and carried back down this chain by the hive edge. The night knows
# nothing about who was there; the row does, because the turn that opened the
# generation declared it (ADR-0002 E8). Nothing here derives or widens it.
audience = str(ctx.get("keeper_audience", "") or "")

FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
now_dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
now = now_dt.strftime(FMT)
# Fixed-width UTC stamps order lexicographically, so "older than" is a store
# comparison and no timestamp is ever parsed on the row side.
cutoff = (now_dt - datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=IDLE_MS)).strftime(FMT)

COLUMNS = ["channel", "session_id", "opened_at", "last_seen", "closed", "closed_at",
           "audience_set", "owed_turn", "channel_node"]
HEAL_COLUMNS = ["session_id", "channel", "audience_set", "closed_at", "owed_turn"]

# R-AG-1 (GH #1229): the night has no tick. ./night carries no schedule; this
# pass keeps ONE one-shot under a fixed name and arms it again whenever the
# moment it is for moves: when a generation opens (the first strike of the
# night) and after every firing (the moment the next open generation falls
# silent). A keeper with nothing open arms nothing and stays silent.
NIGHT_WATCHDOG = "night-close"
NIGHT_BODY = {"messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": "night-close"}]}


# >>> watchdog v1 (R-AG-1, GH #1096)
import datetime as _wd_dt
import uuid as _wd_uuid

WATCHDOG_NS = _wd_uuid.UUID("6f1c2a8e-3b7d-5e90-9a41-0c2d7e5b8f13")


def watchdog_id(name):
    """Stable schedule id for a watchdog name: re-arming the name replaces it."""
    return str(_wd_uuid.uuid5(WATCHDOG_NS, str(name)))


def _iso(ms):
    return _wd_dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(
        int(ms) / 1000.0, tz=_wd_dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def once(name, at_ms, emit_to, body, catch_up=True):
    """One-shot watchdog: fires once at `at_ms` (epoch ms). `at_ms` must lie
    ahead: the timer refuses a past moment (`at_in_past`), so a caller whose
    moment has come does the work now instead of arming. `catch_up` (default
    on) fires a moment missed while the colony was down once on its next
    start, with `late: true`; without it a missed watchdog never fires."""
    return {"op": "add", "schedule_id": watchdog_id(name), "schedule_name": str(name),
            "at": _iso(at_ms), "emit_to": emit_to, "emit_body": body,
            "rearm": True, "catch_up": bool(catch_up)}


def retrigger(name, now_ms, quiet_ms, emit_to, body):
    """Debounce: fires `quiet_ms` (> 0) after the last call; every call
    pushes it out. The lead travels as `after_ms` and the timer resolves it
    on its own clock, so it cannot run out in flight; `now_ms` is not read."""
    order = once(name, 0, emit_to, body)
    del order["at"]
    order["after_ms"] = max(1, int(quiet_ms))
    return order


def calendar(name, cron, emit_to, body):
    """Calendar watchdog (Jenkins-style): real calendar points only, never a
    tick. `cron` is the timer's 6-field Quartz form, seconds first, in UTC
    (`0 0 3 * * *`)."""
    return {"op": "add", "schedule_id": watchdog_id(name), "schedule_name": str(name),
            "cron": cron, "emit_to": emit_to, "emit_body": body, "rearm": True}


def cancel(name):
    """Disarm a watchdog by name. A watchdog that is not armed (never armed,
    already fired) answers `timer_op_error` / `schedule_not_found`."""
    return {"op": "remove", "schedule_id": watchdog_id(name)}
# <<< watchdog v1


EPOCH = datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)


def ms_of(dt):
    """`dt` as epoch milliseconds."""
    return (dt - EPOCH) // datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=1)


def in_night(dt):
    """Whether the UTC moment `dt` lies inside the night window."""
    if NIGHT_FROM == NIGHT_UNTIL:
        return False
    m = dt.hour * 60 + dt.minute
    if NIGHT_FROM < NIGHT_UNTIL:
        return NIGHT_FROM <= m < NIGHT_UNTIL
    return m >= NIGHT_FROM or m < NIGHT_UNTIL


def next_night_start(dt):
    """The first moment at or after `dt` that lies in the night: `dt` itself
    when it does, else the next opening of the window. None for an empty
    window -- there is no night to wait for."""
    if NIGHT_FROM == NIGHT_UNTIL:
        return None
    if in_night(dt):
        return dt
    start = dt.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) \
        + datetime.timedelta(minutes=NIGHT_FROM)
    if start < dt:
        start += datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    return start


def arm(at_dt):
    """The one order to ./night: strike ../close at `at_dt`. `rearm` replaces
    whatever the name held, and `catch_up` fires a moment the colony spent
    switched off once on its next start (a `late` strike, below). Every key
    the hive edges read is present and empty, as on `store_op`."""
    order = once(NIGHT_WATCHDOG, ms_of(at_dt), "../close", NIGHT_BODY)
    order["header"] = {"route": "night", "phase": "", "channel": "",
                       "session_id": "", "audience_set": ""}
    order["messages"] = []
    return order


def stamp_at(base, i):
    """`base` plus i microseconds, in the fixed-width form every stamp of this
    hive has. WHY (GH #954, review I-1): the unique index `sessions_open_round`
    is (channel, audience_set, closed_at); a sweep that sealed two generations
    of one round with ONE `now` wrote two rows the index cannot hold, and the
    next wake then failed to create it. A stamp that does not parse (a row
    from an older writer) gets the counter appended instead -- still distinct,
    still never empty."""
    try:
        dt = datetime.datetime.strptime(str(base), FMT).replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    except Exception:
        return str(base) + "+" + str(i) if i else str(base)
    return (dt + datetime.timedelta(microseconds=i)).strftime(FMT)


def park():
    """Terminal by design: a night without an idle channel emits NOTHING, and
    so does a lost guard race."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def store_op(args, ph, sid="", ch=None, aud=None, meta=""):
    """Every emission carries the full key set the hive edges read. A missing
    hop key makes a CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge --
    so keys are always present and empty rather than absent. `keeper_meta` is
    the generation's facts a close reports (GH #1305): the store answers rows,
    not the row a seal was about, so they ride the round trip as context."""
    return {"header": {"route": "kstore", "phase": ph,
                       "channel": channel if ch is None else ch,
                       "session_id": sid,
                       "audience_set": audience if aud is None else aud,
                       "keeper_meta": meta},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "k-" + ph,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def rows_of(doc):
    msgs = doc.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        rows = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []


def leg_errors(doc):
    """(operation, error_code) of the first refused leg of a bundle reply, or
    None. A bundle never refuses wholesale for one leg: the header
    `error_code` stays empty and the refusal sits on the leg (GH #295)."""
    for r in doc.get("results") or []:
        if isinstance(r, dict) and str(r.get("error_code") or ""):
            return str(r.get("operation") or "update"), str(r.get("error_code"))
    return None


def reject(opname, code, ph):
    if ph == "seal":
        state = ("the sweep DID find this channel; only the seal did not take, "
                 "so the generation stays open, no close was asked for, and the "
                 "next firing finds it again -- a refused seal is not the lost "
                 "guard race it looks like")
    elif ph in ("owed", "release"):
        state = ("a sealed generation that still waits for the final answer of "
                 "its last turn was not released, so its close was not asked "
                 "for tonight; the mark stays and the next firing tries again")
    elif ph.startswith("heal"):
        state = ("the heal of old rows did not take on this page (GH #954); "
                 "nothing was deleted and no open generation was touched, and "
                 "the next firing visits the same rows again")
    elif ph == "next":
        state = ("the question for the generation that falls silent next was "
                 "not answered, so no strike was armed for it; the next "
                 "generation that opens arms the night again (GH #1229)")
    else:
        state = ("nothing was swept -- an unanswered sweep is not a night "
                 "without an idle channel, and the next firing is a night away")
    return {"header": {"route": "reject", "reject_reason": "store_refused",
                       "store_error": code, "store_operation": str(opname),
                       "phase": "", "channel": channel, "session_id": session,
                       "audience_set": audience},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "k-reject",
                          "text": "the session store refused the " + str(opname)
                                  + " of step '" + ph + "': " + code + ". "
                                  + state}]}


def close_of(sid, room, round_):
    """The close request for ONE generation; the body carries no turns. Since
    GH #1305 it says why and when (`close_reason`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`)
    and where the person was reached (`channel_node`), read off the facts the
    seal carried through the store (`keeper_meta`); every key is present and
    empty when unknown, like every other hop key of this hive."""
    try:
        meta = json.loads(str(ctx.get("keeper_meta", "") or "{}"))
    except Exception:
        meta = {}
    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
        meta = {}
    return {"header": {"route": "close", "phase": "", "channel": room,
                       "session_id": sid, "audience_set": round_,
                       "close_reason": str(meta.get("reason") or ""),
                       "opened_at": str(meta.get("opened_at") or ""),
                       "closed_at": str(meta.get("closed_at") or ""),
                       "channel_node": str(meta.get("channel_node") or "")},
            "messages": []}


def reason_now():
    """Why this pass closes (GH #1305, OR-agent-2.C3.1): `night` when the
    moment lies in the night window, else `idle` -- a sweep an operator forced
    by day ends a silent generation all the same."""
    return "night" if in_night(now_dt) else "idle"


def meta_of_row(r, closed_at, reason=None):
    """The facts of one generation a close reports, as the `keeper_meta` text.
    `reason` defaults to this pass's own (`reason_now`); the release of an owed
    row passes `round` (GH #1305 review M1, ruling of the wave's orchestrator):
    such a row was sealed by the stamp's `seal-owed`, i.e. by the next round,
    and the night only lets it go -- the reason is the cause, not the moment."""
    return json.dumps({"opened_at": str(r.get("opened_at") or ""),
                       "closed_at": str(closed_at or ""),
                       "channel_node": str(r.get("channel_node") or ""),
                       "reason": reason if reason else reason_now()})


def heal_page():
    """One page of sealed rows the heal has not visited yet (GH #954).
    `owed_turn` IS NULL is the mark: every seal and open since the column
    exists writes a string there, so NULL is exactly a row written before it
    -- the rows that may still collide under `sessions_open_round`."""
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "sessions", "columns": HEAL_COLUMNS,
                     "where": {"closed": 1, "owed_turn": {"is_null": True}},
                     "order_by": [{"col": "closed_at", "dir": "asc"}],
                     "limit": HEAL_LIMIT}, "heal-page", "", "", "")


def heal_marks(rows, more):
    """The heal-mark of a set of sealed rows whose WHOLE collision groups are
    known: within each (channel, audience_set, closed_at) the row with the
    smallest session_id keeps its stamp and every other one gets
    `<closed_at>~<session_id>`: the session id is unique per generation, so
    the new stamp collides with nothing -- a stamp + k microseconds could meet
    a third row already on that instant (review of fix round 1); it still
    sorts right after the old instant. A row not visited
    yet gets `owed_turn` '' (visited). A row that is neither is left alone --
    in particular a visited one's `owed_turn` is never touched. Guarded by
    `closed = 1`: the heal never touches an open generation, and it deletes
    nothing."""
    groups = {}
    for r in rows:
        if not isinstance(r, dict) or not str(r.get("session_id") or ""):
            continue
        key = (str(r.get("channel") or ""), str(r.get("audience_set") or ""),
               r.get("closed_at"))
        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(r)
    legs = []
    for key in sorted(groups, key=lambda k: json.dumps(k)):
        members = sorted(groups[key], key=lambda r: str(r.get("session_id")))
        for k, r in enumerate(members):
            upd = {}
            if r.get("owed_turn") is None:
                upd["owed_turn"] = ""
            if k and r.get("closed_at") is not None:
                upd["closed_at"] = str(r.get("closed_at")) + "~" + str(r.get("session_id"))
            if upd:
                legs.append({"operation": "update", "table": "sessions", "set": upd,
                             "where": {"session_id": str(r.get("session_id")),
                                       "closed": 1}})
    if not legs:
        return []
    msg = store_op(legs[0], "heal-mark-more" if more else "heal-mark", "", "", "")
    msg["messages"] = [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                        "id": "k-heal-mark-%d" % i, "text": json.dumps(a)}
                       for i, a in enumerate(legs)]
    return [msg]


def firing():
    """One firing asks four things, each its own chain:
      sweep      open generations silent past the cutoff -> seal + close.
      owed       the SENTINEL (GH #953): sealed generations that still wait for
                 the final answer of their last turn (`owed_turn` set, see the
                 stamp's `in_answered`) and have been silent past the cutoff.
                 That answer is not coming -- a brain that died, a writer whose
                 `turn_write` is switched off -- so the night releases the mark
                 and sends the close the acknowledgement would have sent.
                 `neq ''` lets no NULL through: a row from before the column
                 owes nothing.
      heal-page  the heal of rows from before the unique index (GH #954), a page
                 at a time until none is left; after that it costs one empty
                 select per firing.
      next       the row that falls silent next (GH #1229), open or sealed: the
                 watchdog is armed for the moment it crosses the threshold. A
                 generation sealed just now without an owed answer costs at most
                 one empty strike."""
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "sessions", "columns": COLUMNS,
                    "where": {"closed": 0, "last_seen": {"lt": cutoff}},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "last_seen", "dir": "asc"}],
                    "limit": CLOSE_LIMIT}, "sweep"),
          store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "sessions", "columns": COLUMNS,
                    "where": {"closed": 1, "owed_turn": {"neq": ""},
                              "last_seen": {"lt": cutoff}},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "last_seen", "dir": "asc"}],
                    "limit": CLOSE_LIMIT}, "owed"),
          heal_page(),
          store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "sessions", "columns": ["last_seen"],
                    "where": {"last_seen": {"gte": cutoff}},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "last_seen", "dir": "asc"}],
                    "limit": 1}, "next", "", "", "")])


# ================================================================== REFUSED
# A store refusal is not a result, and it sits AHEAD of the firing and the
# phases. Both measured failures are silent ones, and both look exactly like a
# correct night: a refused `sweep` comes back as an empty row list, which reads
# as "no channel was idle", and a refused `seal` comes back with
# `rows_affected` 0, which reads as the lost guard race the seal is written to
# tolerate. A night that could not run must SAY so -- it runs once, and the
# next one is 24 hours away. A refused LEG of a bundle (the heal marks) is a
# refusal too, though the header carries no error_code for it.
if err and op:
    emit([reject(op, err, phase)])
if op == "bundle" and leg_errors(d):
    emit([reject(leg_errors(d)[0], leg_errors(d)[1], phase)])

# ==================================================================== THE ARM
# The event that arms the night (GH #1229): the store wrote a generation. Two
# writes do that, and the hive carries the reply of each here as well as back
# to its writer: the stamp's insert of a NEW generation (phase `open`), and the
# porter's import of a `sessions` row (phase `import`, review K-UHREN A I1) --
# an import carries open generations exactly as they stand, and the receiving
# keeper continues them without an `open` of its own, so without this second
# way an imported keeper never ended a session. Outside the night it arms the
# watchdog for the next opening of the window -- every write of the day names
# the same moment, and re-arming the same moment changes nothing. Inside the
# night it IS a firing: the moment has already come, and the timer would
# refuse it (`at_in_past`). A keeper whose window is empty arms nothing.
if phase in ("open", "import") and op == "insert":
    if rows_affected < 1:
        park()
    first = next_night_start(now_dt)
    if first is None:
        park()
    if not in_night(now_dt):
        emit([arm(first)])
    # The keys in context name the turn that opened a generation, not a
    # generation this firing is about.
    channel, session, audience = "", "", ""
    firing()

# ================================================================== THE FIRING
# Two ways in besides the arm above, both explicit: the strike of the night
# watchdog (it names itself in the auto headers) and a port lane for an
# operator-forced sweep. Anything else is not a firing -- the close pass shares
# a store with the stamp, and a stray message must never seal a channel at noon.
#
# A LATE strike (GH #922: its moment passed while the colony was down, and
# `catch_up` fired it on the next start) that lands outside the night ends no
# session -- that would be a seal at noon. It arms the next night instead.
if lane == "in_sweep" or str(hop.get("schedule_name", "") or ""):
    if op is not None:
        park()
    if hop.get("late") is True and not in_night(now_dt):
        first = next_night_start(now_dt)
        if first is None:
            park()
        emit([arm(first)])
    firing()

# =================================================================== PHASES
if phase == "sweep" and op == "select" and not err:
    out = []
    for r in rows_of(d):
        sid = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
        if not sid:
            continue
        # Guarded: closed = 0 in the where clause is what makes a second
        # firing (or a second sweep of the same night) affect zero rows. The
        # stamp is distinct per row of this firing (`stamp_at`, GH #954), and
        # the mark of an owed answer goes with the seal: two hours of silence
        # mean no answer is coming any more (GH #953).
        at = stamp_at(now, len(out))
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "sessions",
                             "set": {"closed": 1, "closed_at": at,
                                     "owed_turn": ""},
                             "where": {"session_id": sid, "closed": 0}},
                            "seal", sid, str(r.get("channel") or ""),
                            str(r.get("audience_set") or ""), meta_of_row(r, at)))
    emit(out)

if phase == "seal" and op == "update" and not err:
    if rows_affected < 1:
        park()
    # The generation is over. What happens with the day belongs to the
    # collector: it reads its own store and emits the batch.
    emit([close_of(session, channel, audience)])

if phase == "owed" and op == "select" and not err:
    out = []
    for r in rows_of(d):
        sid = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
        owed = str(r.get("owed_turn") or "")
        if not sid or not owed:
            continue
        # Guarded on the mark itself: the acknowledgement of a late answer and
        # this release clear the SAME value, and only the one that clears it
        # sends the close.
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "sessions",
                             "set": {"owed_turn": ""},
                             "where": {"session_id": sid, "closed": 1, "owed_turn": owed}},
                            "release", sid, str(r.get("channel") or ""),
                            str(r.get("audience_set") or ""),
                            meta_of_row(r, r.get("closed_at"), "round")))
    emit(out)

if phase == "release" and op == "update" and not err:
    if rows_affected < 1:
        park()
    emit([close_of(session, channel, audience)])

if phase == "heal-page" and op == "select" and not err:
    page = [r for r in rows_of(d) if isinstance(r, dict) and str(r.get("session_id") or "")]
    if not page:
        # The old rows are healed; the next wake creates the index.
        park()
    more = len(rows_of(d)) >= HEAL_LIMIT
    stamps = sorted({r.get("closed_at") for r in page if r.get("closed_at") is not None})
    loose = [r for r in page if r.get("closed_at") is None]
    out = []
    if stamps:
        # Every sealed row under one of these stamps -- visited ones included,
        # since a partner of a row on this page may have been visited before.
        peers = store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "sessions",
                          "columns": HEAL_COLUMNS,
                          "where": {"closed": 1, "closed_at": {"in": stamps}}},
                         "heal-peers-more" if more else "heal-peers", "", "", "")
        out.append(peers)
    # A row without a stamp collides with nothing (NULL is distinct in a
    # unique index); it is only marked visited.
    out += heal_marks(loose, more and not stamps)
    emit(out)

if phase in ("heal-peers", "heal-peers-more") and op == "select" and not err:
    emit(heal_marks(rows_of(d), phase == "heal-peers-more"))

if phase in ("heal-mark", "heal-mark-more") and op in ("update", "bundle") and not err:
    # A full page may have a next one; a short page was the last.
    if phase == "heal-mark-more":
        emit([heal_page()])
    park()

if phase == "next" and op == "select" and not err:
    # The strike for the row that falls silent next: one millisecond past its
    # threshold, so the firing it starts finds it on the `lt` side -- never
    # sooner than a second from now (the order must still lie ahead when the
    # timer reads it), and never outside the night: a moment of the day waits
    # for the next opening of the window. No row, nothing open: nothing armed.
    row = next((r for r in rows_of(d) if isinstance(r, dict)), None)
    try:
        seen = datetime.datetime.strptime(str((row or {}).get("last_seen")), FMT) \
            .replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        park()
    at_ms = max(ms_of(seen) + IDLE_MS + 1, ms_of(now_dt) + 1000)
    at = EPOCH + datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=at_ms)
    if not in_night(at):
        at = next_night_start(at)
        if at is None:
            park()
    emit([arm(at)])

park()

idle_ms.description: How long a channel has to stay silent before a nightly firing ends its generation. Two hours by default; the cutoff is now minus this value and the comparison runs in the store. Since session-keeper@2.2.0 it is a param of this cell rather than an environment token (GH #138), so two keepers in one colony can end their sessions on different rules.

close_limit.description: How many generations one firing may seal. The runaway guard of the sweep: a store select has no implicit limit. What a firing does not reach waits for the next strike (README, Known limits). A param since session-keeper@2.2.0 (GH #138).

heal_limit.description: How many sealed rows written before `owed_turn` existed one heal page visits (GH #954). The heal makes every (channel, audience_set, closed_at) unique again -- the smallest session_id keeps its stamp, every other one gets `<closed_at>~<session_id>`, unique by its session id -- so the unique index `sessions_open_round` can be created on the next wake. A full page asks for the next one in the same firing; once nothing is left, a firing costs one empty select. Nothing is deleted and no open row is touched.

night_from_utc.description: Where the night begins, as "HH:MM" of the UTC day. With `night_until_utc` it is the window [from, until) in which a generation silent past `idle_ms` ends; it crosses midnight when from is later than until, and from equal to until is no night at all (nothing is armed; an `in_sweep` still sweeps). Since GH #1229 the night is a watchdog this cell arms on `./night` (R-AG-1), not a cron of the timer. The default is the UTC image of 00:00 Europe/Berlin in SUMMER (CEST, UTC+2): 22:00. Winter (CET, UTC+1) is "23:00". Compute your own: UTC = local - offset, and an hour below zero wraps into the day before (00:00 CEST - 2 h = 22:00 UTC of the previous day).

night_until_utc.description: Where the night ends, as "HH:MM" of the UTC day, exclusive; "24:00" is the end of the day. The default is the UTC image of 06:00 Europe/Berlin in summer (CEST, UTC+2): 04:00, so the shipped night is 00:00 until 06:00 local. Winter (CET, UTC+1) is "05:00". No strike lands outside the window: a generation that falls silent by day ends at the next opening of the night.

keeper_meta.description: GH #1305: on `kstore` the facts of the generation the close will report, as JSON text (`opened_at`, `closed_at`, `channel_node`, `reason`), carried through the store as `context.keeper_meta`.

close_reason.description: on `close` why the generation ended (GH #1305): `night` when the firing lies in the night window, `idle` for a sweep forced outside it, `round` on the release of an owed row (a turn of another round sealed it; the cause wins over the moment) `shutdown` is reserved for a keeper that ends its generations on the way down; nothing sends it today.

opened_at.description: on `close` the instant the generation opened, off its row (GH #1305)

closed_at.description: on `close` the instant the generation was sealed (GH #1305)

channel_node.description: on `close` the channel cell the generation's turns came in by (GH #1305); empty when unknown

description.purpose: The end of a session, decided by arithmetic: on every nightly firing it asks which channels have been silent longer than the idle threshold, seals those generations under a guard, and asks for exactly one close per generation. No model is consulted about whether a conversation is over. Since GH #953 the same firing also releases a sealed generation whose last turn waited for a final answer that never came (`owed_turn` still set past the idle threshold) and closes it, and since GH #954 it heals sealed rows from before the unique index `sessions_open_round`, a page at a time, without deleting any. Since GH #1229 (R-AG-1) the night has no tick: this pass keeps ONE one-shot on `./night` (`night-close`, `rearm`, `catch_up`) and arms it again whenever its moment moves -- when the stamp writes a new generation by day, for the next opening of the night window, and after every firing, for the moment the generation that falls silent next crosses the idle threshold. A generation opened inside the window is a firing at once, and a keeper with nothing open arms nothing.
description.use_when: Inside the session-keeper hive, fed by the night watchdog it arms itself and by the stamp's insert of every new generation. Wire its 'close' exit to the port that consumes a finished session (the collector's in_close lane).
description.not_in_scope: No summary, no extraction, no memory write: the close pass says WHICH session ended, never what it was worth. No deletes -- a sealed generation keeps its row, which is exactly what makes a repeated firing silent. No tick: nothing fires through a night without an open generation. A strike missed while the colony was down fires once, late, on its next start; outside the night such a strike seals nothing and only arms the next night. And no provenance of its own: the room and the round of a close are READ off the row, never derived from the session_id prefix and never defaulted.
description.emits_meaning: route kstore: the store ops of the current step (hop.phase carries the step; hop.channel, hop.session_id and hop.audience_set are promoted to context by the hive edge, so each seal runs down its own chain). route close: the close request for ONE generation (from a seal of the sweep, or from a release of an owed answer) - hop.session_id names it, hop.channel names the room it was held in, hop.audience_set names the round it was spoken to, and the body carries no turns because the consumer reads the session out of its own store. All three come off the row; an unrecorded round stays EMPTY and is never invented. route reject: the session store refused an op of this chain (hop.reject_reason 'store_refused', hop.store_error the store's own error_code -- a free string, because the store's code list is open -- and hop.store_operation the refused op). The body names the STEP that was refused: at 'sweep' nothing was swept (an unanswered sweep is not a night without an idle channel); at 'seal' the sweep DID find the channel and only the seal did not take, so the generation stays open, no close is asked for, and the next firing finds it again -- which is not the lost guard race a zero rows_affected looks like; at 'owed' and 'release' a waiting generation was not released tonight; at a 'heal-*' step a heal page did not take, and a refused leg of the heal-mark bundle is a reject as well, though the reply's header carries no error_code for it. route night (GH #1229): the one watchdog order for `./night` -- op `add`, schedule `night-close`, `at` in UTC, `rearm` and `catch_up` -- which the hive edge draws to the timer; hop.phase, hop.channel, hop.session_id and hop.audience_set ride on it empty.
description.consumes_meaning: A firing is recognised by hop.schedule_name (the watchdog names its own schedule; a `hop.late` strike outside the night only arms the next night), by the in_sweep port lane, or by the stamp's successful insert of a new generation (context.store_origin 'keeper-stamp', context.ses_phase 'open', GH #1229), which inside the night is a firing and outside it arms the watchdog; anything else is parked. Store replies are dispatched by context.ses_phase together with hop.operation, context.channel and context.keeper_audience carry the room and the round of the generation being sealed, and hop.rows_affected on the guarded update decides who owns the close - exactly once per generation.
examples: 14:00 UTC, tg:42 opens a generation -> one order to ./night: `night-close` at 22:00:00.000000Z; every further open of that day names the same moment and changes nothing

22:00 UTC, the strike; tg:42 fell silent at 20:10 -> update closed=1 where session_id and closed=0 -> rows_affected 1 -> one close request for tg:42-<opened_at>, carrying the room and the round that row was opened with; `next` finds no row still inside the idle window, and nothing is armed
23:30 UTC, the same channel again -> the select no longer sees it (closed = 1), so the repeated firing is silent

23:00 UTC, tg:42's generation was sealed by a turn of a new round at 20:10 and its last answer never arrived (owed_turn 'tg:42/t-17') -> update owed_turn='' where session_id, closed=1 and owed_turn='tg:42/t-17' -> rows_affected 1 -> one close request, carrying the room and the round off the row

first firing after an upgrade, two sealed rows of tg:42 share closed_at 2026-09-01T23:00:00.000000Z -> the smaller session_id keeps it, the other becomes 2026-09-01T23:00:00.000000Z~<its session_id>, both get owed_turn '' -> the next wake creates sessions_open_round; later firings find no unvisited row and park
23:15 UTC, tg:7 opens a generation inside the night -> the firing runs at once; `next` finds tg:7 at 23:15 and arms the strike for 01:15:00.001 UTC
the colony was down at 22:00 and starts at 09:00 UTC -> the missed strike fires late -> no sweep at noon, one order for 22:00 UTC
